title: Random forest separates Escherichia cryptic clade II genomes by habitat
summary: A random forest classifier was trained on delta bitscore functional-divergence metrics from Escherichia genomes, including strains with known habitat adaptation, to separate gastrointestinal from external-environment genomes. The model correctly classified the genomes and identified predictor genes informative of habitat association, with gene degradation more prominent in gastrointestinal strains. It correctly predicted habitats of an independent set of strains with known habitat. The authors describe the evidence as preliminary indications of divergent niche adaptation.
